steps.what: Open postage rates, regulations, and procedures

tasks.design: Postage rates, regulations, and procedures are opened from {DOCS}. The clerk answers the customer's questions, including questions about office boxes. The page is a reference. It does not speak to the customer.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk left the counter to find a rate or a box rule.
tasks.enabler_now: The rate and the box rule are on the counter screen.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining a rule, and saying when it does not fit, stays with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk hears the actual question.

ambition.what: A rate or a box rule that is already written can be answered in the same visit, and the clerk still speaks.

tasks.altitude: The clerk has the page before answering.

evidence.claim: A stored rate or procedure page can be opened for a named question. Speaking the answer stays with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a customer asks and ends when the clerk has answered or said the rule does not cover it.
A page has a rule id and text, written by the operations owner. A question with no rule id is not given a generated answer.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the question is not covered by a written rule.
research_questions: Which questions used a stored page, and which the clerk answered without one?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most questions are not on a page. High: the rate or box rule is already written and the clerk only explains it. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the next station for this mail
Transport mail from one station to another

tasks.design: The next station for the bundle is shown from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The clerk transports the mail from one station to another. The screen does not move the mail.
tasks.previous_blocker: The next station was a handwritten tag.
tasks.enabler_now: The station name is on the bundle.
tasks.still_hard: Carrying the mail stays with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: Nothing about the carrying changes. The tag is only easier to read.

evidence.claim: A stored station name can be shown on a bundle. Carrying the mail stays with the person. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a bundle is ready to move and ends when it is at the next station.
A bundle row has bundle id and next station, set by the sort plan.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the next station is missing.
research_questions: Which bundles had a station name, and which the clerk had to ask about?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the station is missing and the clerk must ask. High: the name is on the bundle and the carrying remains. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open prices for stamps, prepaid envelopes, and money orders
Sell products and collect the payment

tasks.design: Prices for stamps, prepaid mail envelopes, and money orders are opened from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The clerk sells the product and collects the payment into {BANK}. A product with no price is not sold. The screen does not take the money.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices were a card at the drawer, and the clerk re-read them.
tasks.enabler_now: The price is on the product.
tasks.still_hard: Handing over the product and taking the money stay with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees the note and the product.

ambition.what: A priced product can be sold in the same visit, and the clerk still takes the money.

tasks.altitude: The clerk sees the price before taking payment.

evidence.claim: A stored price can be shown for a product id. Taking payment stays with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a customer asks to buy and ends when the clerk has taken payment or refused the sale.
A product row has product id, name, and price, maintained by the pricing owner. A missing price blocks the sale.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often a product has no stored price.
research_questions: Which sales used a stored price, and which the clerk refused?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: The products and the amount the customer paid

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the product has no price and the clerk must stop. High: the price is stored and the clerk still sells and collects. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Record the count and keep money drawers in order
Balance daily transactions and sign the close

tasks.design: Stored daily transactions are totaled in {BANK}. The clerk counts the money drawers, keeps them in order, and records the count. The clerk balances the count to the total and signs the close. A difference is not written off by the screen.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk added the day's slips by hand before counting the drawer.
tasks.enabler_now: The transactions are already stored, so the total is the sum of those rows.
tasks.still_hard: Counting the notes and deciding what a difference means stay with the clerk.

ambition.what: The stored total is ready when the drawer is counted, and the clerk still signs the close.

tasks.altitude: The clerk sees the total before signing.

evidence.claim: A total of stored transactions is arithmetic. Counting cash and signing a difference stay with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when the counter day ends and ends when the clerk has signed the close or marked a difference.
A transaction row has day, amount, and tender, written when the clerk took payment. The total ignores a row with no amount.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often a payment was never stored.
research_questions: Which days matched, and which the clerk marked as a difference?

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: The counted drawer total beside the stored daily transactions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many payments were never stored, so the total is not the drawer. High: the rows are complete and the clerk only counts and signs. The range stays under the net.

role.altitude: The clerk still answers, carries mail, sells, and counts the drawer. A stored price or a stored total is on the screen first.
reach: A supervisor can see the signed drawer close for that day.
skills_to_grow: Explain a rule the page does not quite fit.
role.ambitious_version: Priced products and stored totals are ready the same day. The clerk still speaks, carries, takes money, and signs the close.
